Thanks again for the conversation earlier, Ana and Michael — good to meet you both. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can scope a tidy cost proposal and POC: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: generative completions for user-facing features (~50M tokens/mo estimate) + embeddings for search/ranking (~10M embeddings/mo).
- Residency: EU residency required for EU users; US residency acceptable for US users (data partitioning preferred).
- Procurement timeline: POC in May, production decision in Q3 if the economics line up.

Clarifying asks (one-line answers are perfect):
1) Can you confirm the monthly token volume bands (low/expected/high) you want us to model? e.g., 20/50/100M tokens.
2) Target unit economics: what is your target $/1M tokens or budget range for the hosted tier?
3) Any constraints on encryption/KMS or support SLAs beyond standard enterprise?

What we'll do next:
- Send a short cost model showing US vs EU hosted unit rates and an optional reserved-capacity scenario (savings with commit).
- Map an EU-residency uplift and call out any compliance/observability artifacts you’ll need for procurement.
- Propose 2 dates for a deeper procurement/demo discussion.

Attachments: RWI-pricing-playbook.pdf (high-level bands & reserved-capacity examples)

Thanks, Ava — great recap. Quick answers below so you can build the model: 

1) Volume bands (monthly tokens): low 25M, expected 55M, high 120M. These are aggregate gen tokens; embeddings are separate (see #2).
2) Embeddings: expect ~8–12M embedding requests/month at ~1k tokens per request (we can normalize in your model).
3) Budget/target: for hosted like-for-like we’re targeting ~$1,200 per 1M gen tokens as our internal benchmark. If EU-residency adds significant uplift, call it out — we’d prefer <15% uplift if possible.
4) KMS: we use a centralized KMS (AWS KMS) and will require customer-managed keys for the production environment.

Procurement notes: finance will want a clear per-region comparison and an option that shows a committed reserved tier (12-month) vs on-demand. POC can run on hosted EU region if the residency model is clear.

I attached a short doc with POC requirements. Happy to hop on another call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Ava / Jonas — taking Ana's numbers and drafting a quick unit-econ note for the team before we send the external model. Notes: 

Assumptions from Ana: expected 55M gen tokens/mo, 10M embeddings/mo. Target $1,200 / 1M gen tokens (benchmark). KMS customer-managed. EU residency required for EU users.

Preliminary pricing bands (hosted):
- On-demand US: $1,200 / 1M gen tokens
- On-demand EU: apply a 10% regional uplift -> $1,320 / 1M gen tokens (covers infra variance, egress, and higher SLAs for EU residency).
- Reserved (12mo commit) US: $950 / 1M (approx 20% discount with 70% commit utilization).
- Reserved (12mo commit) EU: $1,045 / 1M (same discount applied to uplifted rate).

Embeddings: price separately; approximate band $0.30–$0.45 per 1k embedding vectors depending on quantization and cache hit rate.

Quick back-of-envelope for expected band (expected 55M gen tokens + 10M embeddings):
- Gen tokens cost (US on-demand): 55 * $1.2k = $66k / month -> $792k / year
- Gen tokens cost (EU on-demand): 55 * $1.32k = $72.6k / month -> $871.2k / year
- Embeddings: 10M * $0.35 /1k = $3.5k / month -> $42k / year (rough)

Key tradeoffs to call out to FinOps Labs:
- Reserved offers material savings for sustained workloads; worth asking for a 12mo/24mo commit scenario in the model.
- EU uplift is primarily infra/egress + compliance staffing/time; engineering can mitigate some with edge caching and prefix/KV cache config.
- Customer-managed KMS: small per-region operational premium to provide HSM/KMS integration and audit logs.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Build a short spreadsheet with US vs EU on-demand and reserved rows + turnkey assumptions. (I'll start the sheet and share.)
2) Ava to send external note that proposes the US/EU bands and asks Ana to confirm which region(s) will be production-critical first.

I'll attach the regional-cost-model.xlsx once I finish.
